name: Git & Version Control
description: Tracking changes, branching, merging and collaborating on code with Git and remote repositories.

questions.question: Which command creates a new, empty Git repository in the current directory?
questions.explanation: git init creates the .git directory that turns the folder into a repository.

questions.question: Which command stages all changes in the current directory for the next commit?
questions.explanation: git add . adds changes under the current directory to the staging area (index).

questions.question: What is the difference between git fetch and git pull?
options: fetch downloads remote changes without integrating them; pull fetches and then merges or rebases them into the current branch
fetch uploads commits; pull downloads them
pull only works on the main branch
questions.explanation: git pull is essentially git fetch followed by git merge (or rebase); fetch leaves your working branch untouched.

questions.question: Which command undoes the last local commit but keeps its changes staged?
questions.explanation: --soft moves the branch pointer back but leaves the index and working tree intact; --hard discards changes and revert creates a new commit.

questions.question: Why should you avoid rebasing commits that are already pushed to a shared branch?
options: Rebasing rewrites commits with new hashes, so collaborators' histories diverge from the rewritten one
Rebase cannot be used with remote branches
questions.explanation: Rewritten history forces others to reconcile duplicate or missing commits and requires force-pushing.

questions.question: Which command uses binary search through history to find the commit that introduced a bug?
questions.explanation: git bisect checks out midpoints between a known good and bad commit until the first bad commit is identified.

practical.title: Feature branch workflow
practical.instructions: Write the sequence of Git commands to: create and switch to a branch named feature/login, stage the file login.py, commit it with a message, and push the branch to origin while setting the upstream.
practical.expected_output: git checkout -b feature/login (or git switch -c), git add login.py, git commit -m "...", git push -u origin feature/login.

rubric.hint: Use git checkout -b feature/login or git switch -c feature/login.
Stage the file with git add login.py.
Use git push -u origin feature/login to set the upstream.

tasks.title: Read Git basics
tasks.description: Read chapters 1 and 2 of Pro Git (Getting Started and Git Basics). Set up your name and email and practise init, status, add, commit and log in a test folder.
tasks.completion_criteria: A local repo with at least 5 commits and a clean git status.

tasks.title: Complete Learn Git Branching introduction
tasks.description: Complete the Introduction Sequence and Ramping Up levels on Learn Git Branching. Focus on branch, merge, rebase and HEAD movement.
tasks.completion_criteria: All levels in the first two sections completed.

tasks.title: Resolve merge conflicts and use remotes
tasks.description: Push a repo to a hosting service, create two branches that edit the same lines and resolve the conflict. Practise fetch, pull, stash and reset in the process.
tasks.completion_criteria: Remote repo shows a merge commit resolving a real conflict.

tasks.title: Run a pull-request workflow on a team project
tasks.description: With a classmate or an open-source project, work through feature branches, pull requests, code review and an interactive rebase to clean up history before merging. Use git bisect once to locate a deliberately introduced bug.
tasks.completion_criteria: At least 2 merged pull requests with review comments, plus notes from a successful bisect session.
